text:
kevin: Heads-up — merchant 'ArcadiaApps' reporting a spike in card declines since 09:15 UTC. Customers see 3DS pass but issuer declines with AVS result 'C' and CVV result 'M'. Example: auth code Z3. Can we triage? :eyes:

payments-bot: [auto] ticket #INC-4721 created for merchant ArcadiaApps — routing to support-tier2.

maria: Can you paste the gateway request/response for one failing txn (mask PAN)? Also: is this happening across multiple BINs/acquirers or one acquirer?

kevin: Quick sample from the gateway logs (masked):
```
REQUEST -> {"merchant_id":"arcadia_7","amount":4500,"currency":"GBP","card":{"pan":"**** **** **** 4242","exp":"12/26","cvv":"***","billing":{"line1":"Flat 3, 12 High St","city":"Bristol","postcode":"BS1 5TG"}}}
RESPONSE <- {"status":"declined","reason_code":"Z3","avs":"C","cvv":"M","3ds":"authenticated","acquirer":"acq-alpha"}
```

kevin: Repro notes: customer used postcode with space ("BS1 5TG"). When we remove space to "BS15TG" some txns go through. Seems like AVS normalization mismatch between us and acquirer. Happening ~37 txns in last hour.

maria: thx. Which deployment is the merchant on (hosted/dedicated/private)? Do they use PO box or special VAT rules?

kevin: Hosted. No PO box. VAT not relevant. They also saw a couple of recoverable successes when we retried with normalized postcode.

jess: :wave: From runtime side — AVS failures with 3DS success usually indicate issuer side address check is more strict than our normalization. Two quick checks: 1) what normalization profile did we apply on billing.postcode? (we have country-specific rules) 2) which acquirer mapping is in play — some acquirers expect no spaces for UK postcodes.

jess: Can you run a repro curl (masked) and post the full request we send to acq-alpha? Example curl to reproduce: 
```
curl -X POST https://int-api.redwood/payments/charge \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"merchant_id":"arcadia_7","amount":4500,"currency":"GBP","card":{"pan":"4242424242424242","exp":"12/26","cvv":"123","billing":{"postcode":"BS1 5TG","line1":"Flat 3, 12 High St"}}}'
```

kevin: Posted sample to the incident ticket. Also adding a failing txn id: txn_20260317_88 (masked).

payments-bot: Added txn_20260317_88 to ticket INC-4721. Related logs attached.

maria: Ops: ops-sre — can you check acq-alpha's recent AVS normalization change? Also any change in header mapping or address format policies?

ops-sre: I can see increased AVS 'C' responses starting 09:07 UTC. No infra deploys on our side. Reaching out to acq-alpha support — cc'ing acquirer ops contact. Meanwhile, two mitigation options: 1) run a server-side re-normalize step for UK postcodes (strip space) before sending, flagging merchant opt-in; 2) implement a short retry path that normalizes postcode and retries on AVS=C + 3DS=authenticated.

jess: Suggestion: implement conservative retry for AVS=C + 3DS auth OK, up to 1 retry with normalized postcode. Add a metric to not create duplicate charges. Also document in console that merchant can opt into postcode normalization.

kevin: I'll ask merchant to opt-in for retries for now. Can we get a quick uplift on retry logic? This is affecting checkout conversion.

maria: I'll open a small PR on the payments proxy to add postcode normalization + a flag. Jess, can you review?

jess: Yep, will review. Quick patch plan: 
- add normalizer module for UK postcodes (strip whitespace, uppercase)
- on AVS=C && 3DS=authenticated -> retry once with normalized billing.postcode (idempotent guard by txn id)
- emit metric payments.avs_retry.count and payments.avs_retry.success

ops-sre: Also received ack from acq-alpha: they tightened AVS matching rules for UK postcodes last night. They're pushing a config that rejects spaces. They suggested merchants should send postcode without spaces. We're negotiating fallback tolerances.

kevin: Merchant is OK with short retry and will update their SDK after we roll fix. Thanks all. :+1:

maria: Assigning to jess for PR, kevin follow up with merchant and update the ticket. I'll mark INC-4721 as investigating.

payments-bot: [auto] INC-4721 status -> investigating; priority -> P1 (conversion impact).
